transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess… I’ve been having trouble staying seated when I’m supposed to. Like in client interviews, tutoring sessions, even book club. I keep getting up, and people are starting to notice that I can’t just sit there and listen.
Does getting up happen mainly when you’re feeling nervous or anxious?
Not mainly, no. It happens in situations where I’m just supposed to stay put and listen—client interviews, tutoring, book club. I’ll get up, and… people have started noticing.
Do you ever have periods where you feel unusually energetic or wired, even when you haven’t had much sleep?
I don’t think so. I mean, I have restless days, but not really like… unusually wired on no sleep. Not that I’ve noticed.
When you’re sitting in those situations, do you feel an inner urge to move?

Yeah… I think so. It’s mostly that I just can’t seem to stay put when I’m supposed to. Like I end up getting up during client interviews or tutoring, even book club. People have noticed I’m not really just sitting and listening.
Do you feel anxious in those situations before you get up?
Not really… I mean, I might feel a little uncomfortable because I know I’m supposed to sit still, but I wouldn’t call it anxiety before I get up.
Did you have this same kind of trouble staying seated when you were a child?

Yeah. From what I remember, and from my report cards, it was the same kind of thing. They’d say I was bright, but I couldn’t stay in my seat or wait my turn. My mother still makes jokes about me pacing around the classroom like it was a crime scene.
Do you often blurt things out or interrupt other people before they finish?

Yeah… I do. I’ll jump in before I really think it through. Like if the junior detectives are talking through a lead, or even if a neighbor’s talking in the hallway, I’ll start asking questions or giving advice. Then afterward I realize I kind of barged into it.
